subproblem.title: Eventual three-term splitting of the localized weighted blow-up integral along C ⊆ M (parent Step 4)
subproblem.statement:
Let Q, n ∈ ℕ. Let M, C ⊆ ℝ^Q be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q) with C ⊆ M. Let θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ, y ∈ ℝ^Q and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ), and write η_t(x) = blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹(x − y). Suppose there is r > 0 with Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞ and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y). Then for all sufficiently small t > 0 (eventually in 𝓝[>] 0):
 ∫_M φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) = θ(y) · ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) dHⁿ(x) + ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x) + ∫_{M∖C} φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dHⁿ(x)
(Bochner set integrals).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (M C : Set (Eucl Q)) (θ : Eucl Q → ℝ) (y : Eucl Q) (φ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Eucl Q) ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → NullMeasurableSet C (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → C ⊆ M → (∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (C ∩ closedBall y r) < ∞ ∧ IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall y r) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∫ x in M, φ (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x) * θ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) = θ y * ∫ x in C, φ (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) + ∫ x in C, φ (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x) * (θ x - θ y) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) + ∫ x in M \ C, φ (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x) * θ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^Q = Eucl Q = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin Q), with Euclidean norm |·|.
- μ := μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^Q. It is a Borel measure, so closed balls are μ-measurable.
- B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ and B_ρ(0) = ball 0 ρ.
- For t ∈ ℝ, η_t(x) := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹ • (x − y).
- φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ) means φ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Eucl Q) ℝ.
- ∫_S f dμ is the Bochner integral of f against μ restricted to S (it is 0 when f is not integrable on S).
- 'For all sufficiently small t > 0' means 'eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0'.

Fix r > 0 with μ(C ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞ and θ μ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y). Write B_r := B̄_r(y); it is closed, hence measurable.

1. (Constants attached to φ.) tsupport φ is compact, hence bounded, so there is R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball_lt with lower bound 0 and centre 0). φ is continuous with compact support, so there is A ∈ ℝ with |φ(z)| ≤ A for all z (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).

2. (Choice of t.) The map t ↦ tR is continuous with value 0 at t = 0, so tR → 0 as t → 0+ (restrict from 𝓝 0 to 𝓝[>] 0 ≤ 𝓝 0). Since r > 0, tR < r for all sufficiently small t > 0. Fix t > 0 with tR < r and prove the identity for this t; that establishes it for all sufficiently small t > 0. Put F(x) := φ(η_t(x)).

3. (Properties of F.)
 (a) F = 0 outside B_r. If F(x) ≠ 0, then η_t(x) ∈ support φ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0). So |t⁻¹ • (x − y)| = t⁻¹|x − y| < R (as t > 0), i.e. |x − y| < tR < r, and x ∈ B_r.
 (b) F is continuous, being φ composed with the continuous affine map x ↦ t⁻¹ • (x − y). Hence F is a.e.-strongly measurable for every measure.
 (c) |F(x)| ≤ A for every x.

4. (F·θ is integrable on M.) θ is integrable on M ∩ B_r, and F is a.e.-strongly measurable with |F| ≤ A. So x ↦ F(x)θ(x) is integrable on M ∩ B_r: a bounded measurable function times an integrable one is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul). If x ∈ M ∖ (M ∩ B_r), then x ∉ B_r, so F(x)θ(x) = 0 by 3(a). M is null-measurable, and a function integrable on M ∩ B_r that vanishes on M ∖ (M ∩ B_r) is integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). Thus F·θ is integrable on M.

5. (F is integrable on C.) μ(C ∩ B_r) < ∞, and F is a.e.-strongly measurable with |F| ≤ A, so F is integrable on C ∩ B_r (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). F vanishes on C ∖ (C ∩ B_r) by 3(a), and C is null-measurable, so F is integrable on C (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).

6. (Derived integrabilities.)
- Since C ⊆ M and M ∖ C ⊆ M (Set.sdiff_subset), step 4 shows F·θ is integrable on C and on M ∖ C (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
- By step 5, θ(y)·F is integrable on C.
- For all x, F(x)(θ(x) − θ(y)) = F(x)θ(x) − θ(y)F(x). So F·(θ − θ(y)) is integrable on C, as a difference of two functions integrable on C.

7. (Splitting M.)
- Since C ⊆ M, M = C ∪ (M ∖ C) (Set.union_sdiff_cancel).
- C and M ∖ C are disjoint, hence a.e.-disjoint.
- M ∖ C is null-measurable as a difference of null-measurable sets (NullMeasurableSet.diff).
F·θ is integrable on both pieces (step 6), so additivity of the set integral over this union (setIntegral_union₀) gives
 ∫_M F θ dμ = ∫_C F θ dμ + ∫_{M∖C} F θ dμ.

8. (Splitting the weight on C.) For every x, F(x)θ(x) = θ(y)F(x) + F(x)(θ(x) − θ(y)). Both summands are integrable on C (step 6), so by linearity of the integral (integral_add, integral_const_mul)
 ∫_C F θ dμ = θ(y) ∫_C F dμ + ∫_C F (θ − θ(y)) dμ.

9. (Conclusion.) Substituting step 8 into step 7 gives
 ∫_M φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ = θ(y) ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) dμ + ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y)) dμ + ∫_{M∖C} φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ
for every t > 0 with tR < r, and hence for all sufficiently small t > 0. This is the claimed eventual identity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) and A ≥ |φ|. For small t > 0 we have tR < r, and F := φ∘η_t is continuous, satisfies |F| ≤ A, and vanishes off B̄_r(y).
F·θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y) (Integrable.bdd_mul) and vanishes on M ∖ B̄_r(y), so it is integrable on the null-measurable set M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).
F is integrable on C ∩ B̄_r(y) (bounded on a finite-measure set), and hence on C.
Restricting to C and M ∖ C: F·θ is integrable on both, and θ(y)F and F(θ − θ(y)) = Fθ − θ(y)F are integrable on C.
Since M = C ∪ (M ∖ C) is a disjoint union with M ∖ C null-measurable, ∫_M Fθ = ∫_C Fθ + ∫_{M∖C} Fθ (setIntegral_union₀).
On C, Fθ = θ(y)F + F(θ − θ(y)), so ∫_C Fθ = θ(y)∫_C F + ∫_C F(θ − θ(y)) (integral_add, integral_const_mul). Combining gives the identity for all small t > 0.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type match with all hypotheses explicit. Compact support localizes the integrands; local integrability and finite measure establish every integrability needed for extension by zero and integral additivity. Null-measurability and inclusion justify the disjoint partition. The supplied proof establishes the exact eventual identity without circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Continuity of θ along C at y plus bounded upper n-density of C at y: the weight-oscillation blow-up term vanishes (parent Step 6, I₂ → 0)
subproblem.statement:
Let Q, n ∈ ℕ. Let C ⊆ ℝ^Q be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q), θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ, y ∈ ℝ^Q and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ), and write η_t(x) = blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹(x − y). Assume:
- θ restricted to C is continuous at y (ContinuousWithinAt θ C y; y need not lie in C);
- there is K ∈ ℝ≥0 with Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K · ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0.
Then (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x) → 0 as t → 0+. The integral is the Bochner set integral, and no integrability is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (C : Set (Eucl Q)) (θ : Eucl Q → ℝ) (y : Eucl Q) (φ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Eucl Q) ℝ), NullMeasurableSet C (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → ContinuousWithinAt θ C y → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (C ∩ closedBall y ρ) ≤ K * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) → Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => (t ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ x in C, φ (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x) * (θ x - θ y) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^Q = Eucl Q = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin Q), with Euclidean norm |·|.
- μ := μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^Q. It is a Borel measure, so closed balls are μ-measurable.
- B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ and B_ρ(0) = ball 0 ρ.
- For t ∈ ℝ, η_t(x) := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹ • (x − y).
- ∫_S f dμ is the Bochner integral of f against μ restricted to S (0 when f is not integrable on S); ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued lintegral.
- ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is a ↦ max(a, 0). toReal : [0, ∞] → ℝ is the identity on [0, ∞) and sends ∞ to 0.
- 'For all sufficiently small t > 0' means 'eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0'.

Let K ∈ ℝ≥0 be as in the hypothesis, so μ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K · ofReal(ρⁿ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0.

1. (Constants attached to φ.) tsupport φ is compact, hence bounded, so there is R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball_lt). φ is continuous with compact support, so there is A with |φ(z)| ≤ A for all z (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). In particular A ≥ |φ(0)| ≥ 0.

2. (Localization.) Let t > 0 and x ∉ B̄_{tR}(y); then φ(η_t(x)) = 0. Otherwise η_t(x) ∈ support φ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0), so t⁻¹|x − y| < R, i.e. |x − y| < tR, contradicting x ∉ B̄_{tR}(y).

3. (Composition with t ↦ tR.) The map t ↦ tR is continuous, vanishes at 0, and maps (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) because R > 0. So tR → 0 within (0, ∞) as t → 0+ (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Hence the density bound holds at ρ = tR for all sufficiently small t > 0:
 μ(C ∩ B̄_{tR}(y)) ≤ K · ofReal((tR)ⁿ).   (∗)
Also, for every δ > 0, tR < δ for all sufficiently small t > 0.

4. (ε-formulation.) We verify the metric definition of convergence to 0 (Metric.tendsto_nhds). Let ε > 0. Put c := A · K · Rⁿ ≥ 0 and ε₁ := ε / (2(c + 1)) > 0. By ContinuousWithinAt θ C y (Metric.continuousWithinAt_iff) there is δ > 0 such that |θ(x) − θ(y)| < ε₁ for every x ∈ C with |x − y| < δ. By step 3, all sufficiently small t > 0 satisfy both (∗) and tR < δ; fix such a t > 0. It suffices to show
 |(tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y)) dμ(x)| < ε.

5. (Pointwise bound.) C is null-measurable, so μ⌞C-almost every x lies in C (ae_restrict_mem₀). Let x ∈ C.
- If x ∈ B̄_{tR}(y), then |x − y| ≤ tR < δ, so |θ(x) − θ(y)| < ε₁ and |φ(η_t(x))(θ(x) − θ(y))| = |φ(η_t(x))| · |θ(x) − θ(y)| ≤ A ε₁.
- If x ∉ B̄_{tR}(y), then φ(η_t(x)) = 0 by step 2.
Hence, μ⌞C-a.e.,
 ofReal|φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y))| ≤ 1_{B̄_{tR}(y)}(x) · ofReal(A ε₁).

6. (Lintegral bound.) Integrate step 5 over C (lintegral_mono_ae). The closed ball B := B̄_{tR}(y) is measurable, so ∫⁻_C 1_B · ofReal(A ε₁) dμ = ofReal(A ε₁) · (μ⌞C)(B) = ofReal(A ε₁) · μ(B ∩ C) = ofReal(A ε₁) · μ(C ∩ B) (lintegral_indicator_const, Measure.restrict_apply, Set.inter_comm). Multiplying (∗) by the constant ofReal(A ε₁) then gives
 ∫⁻_C ofReal|φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y))| dμ ≤ ofReal(A ε₁) · μ(C ∩ B̄_{tR}(y)) ≤ ofReal(A ε₁) · K · ofReal((tR)ⁿ).
The right-hand side is finite, being a product of finite elements of [0, ∞].

7. (Bochner bound.) For every function f and set S, |∫_S f dμ| ≤ toReal(∫⁻_S ofReal|f| dμ) (norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm; no integrability is needed). toReal is monotone below a finite value (ENNReal.toReal_mono), so step 6 gives
 |∫_C φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y)) dμ| ≤ toReal(ofReal(A ε₁) · K · ofReal((tR)ⁿ)) = A ε₁ · K · (tR)ⁿ.
The equality uses ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (with A ε₁ ≥ 0 and (tR)ⁿ ≥ 0), and the fact that toReal of the coercion of K is K.

8. (Rescaling.) Since t > 0, tⁿ > 0 and (tR)ⁿ = tⁿ Rⁿ, so
 |(tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C …| = (tⁿ)⁻¹ |∫_C …| ≤ (tⁿ)⁻¹ · A ε₁ K tⁿ Rⁿ = A K Rⁿ · ε₁ = c ε₁ = ε · c / (2(c + 1)).
Since 0 ≤ c < 2(c + 1), we have c / (2(c + 1)) < 1, so c ε₁ < ε (as ε > 0).

9. (Conclusion.) Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) (θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x) → 0 as t → 0+. ∎

Given ε > 0, put c = A K Rⁿ and ε₁ = ε/(2(c+1)). ContinuousWithinAt gives δ > 0 with |θ(x) − θ(y)| < ε₁ for x ∈ C, |x − y| < δ. For small t, also tR < δ.
μ⌞C-a.e. (C is null-measurable), ofReal|φ(η_t x)(θ(x) − θ(y))| ≤ 1_{B̄_{tR}(y)}(x)·ofReal(Aε₁). So the lintegral over C is ≤ ofReal(Aε₁)·Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_{tR}(y)) ≤ ofReal(Aε₁)·K·ofReal((tR)ⁿ) < ∞.
Rescaling: |(tⁿ)⁻¹∫_C …| ≤ cε₁ = εc/(2(c+1)) < ε. Since ε is arbitrary, the term tends to 0.

subproblem.title: Zero θ-weighted n-density of a set D at y makes its normalized blow-up integrals vanish (parent Step 7, I₃ → 0)
subproblem.statement:
Let Q, n ∈ ℕ. Let D ⊆ ℝ^Q be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q), and let θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ satisfy θ(x) ≥ 0 for every x ∈ D. Let y ∈ ℝ^Q and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ), and write η_t(x) = blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹(x − y). Suppose
 (∫⁻_{D ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} ENNReal.ofReal(θ) dHⁿ) / ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) → 0 in [0, ∞] as ρ → 0+.
Then (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_D φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) → 0 in ℝ as t → 0+. Here ∫_D is the Bochner set integral, and no integrability of θ is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (D : Set (Eucl Q)) (θ : Eucl Q → ℝ) (y : Eucl Q) (φ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Eucl Q) ℝ), NullMeasurableSet D (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → (∀ x ∈ D, 0 ≤ θ x) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => (∫⁻ x in D ∩ closedBall y ρ, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) / ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => (t ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ x in D, φ (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x) * θ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^Q = Eucl Q = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin Q), with Euclidean norm |·|.
- μ := μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^Q. It is a Borel measure, so closed balls are μ-measurable.
- B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ and B_ρ(0) = ball 0 ρ.
- For t ∈ ℝ, η_t(x) := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹ • (x − y).
- ∫_S f dμ is the Bochner integral of f against μ restricted to S (0 when f is not integrable on S); ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued lintegral.
- ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is a ↦ max(a, 0). toReal : [0, ∞] → ℝ is the identity on [0, ∞) and sends ∞ to 0.
- 'For all sufficiently small t > 0' means 'eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0'.

Put L(ρ) := ∫⁻_{D ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} ofReal(θ(x)) dμ(x) and q(ρ) := L(ρ) / ofReal(ρⁿ). The hypothesis is q(ρ) → 0 in [0, ∞] as ρ → 0+.

1. (Constants attached to φ.) tsupport φ is compact (φ has compact support), hence bounded, so there is R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball_lt with lower bound 0 and centre 0). φ is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: there is A ∈ ℝ with |φ(z)| ≤ A for all z (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). In particular A ≥ |φ(0)| ≥ 0.

2. (Localization.) Let t > 0 and x ∉ B̄_{tR}(y); then φ(η_t(x)) = 0. Indeed, if φ(η_t(x)) ≠ 0, then η_t(x) ∈ support φ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0). That is, |t⁻¹ • (x − y)| = t⁻¹|x − y| < R, so |x − y| < tR and x ∈ B̄_{tR}(y), a contradiction.

3. (Composition with t ↦ tR.) The map t ↦ tR is continuous with value 0 at t = 0, and it maps (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) because R > 0. Hence tR → 0 within (0, ∞) as t → 0+ (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Composing with the hypothesis, q(tR) → 0 in [0, ∞] as t → 0+. Consequently:
 (a) since 0 < ∞, q(tR) < ∞ for all sufficiently small t > 0;
 (b) toReal is continuous at 0 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so toReal(q(tR)) → 0, and therefore b(t) := A · Rⁿ · toReal(q(tR)) → A · Rⁿ · 0 = 0 as t → 0+.

4. (Reduction.) By the squeeze theorem for norms (squeeze_zero_norm'), it suffices to show that for all sufficiently small t > 0
 |(tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_D φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ(x)| ≤ b(t).
By 3(a), we may fix t > 0 with q(tR) < ∞.

5. (L(tR) is finite.) Since tR > 0, (tR)ⁿ > 0, so c := ofReal((tR)ⁿ) satisfies 0 < c < ∞. If L(tR) = ∞, then q(tR) = ∞ / c = ∞ (ENNReal.top_div_of_ne_top), contradicting q(tR) < ∞. Hence L(tR) < ∞.

6. (Pointwise bound.) D is null-measurable, so μ⌞D-almost every x belongs to D (ae_restrict_mem₀). Let x ∈ D.
- If x ∈ B̄_{tR}(y): θ(x) ≥ 0 and |φ(η_t(x))| ≤ A give |φ(η_t(x)) θ(x)| = |φ(η_t(x))| θ(x) ≤ A θ(x). So ofReal|φ(η_t(x)) θ(x)| ≤ ofReal(A θ(x)) = ofReal(A) · ofReal(θ(x)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, using A ≥ 0).
- If x ∉ B̄_{tR}(y): φ(η_t(x)) = 0 by step 2, so the left side is 0.
Hence, μ⌞D-a.e.,
 ofReal|φ(η_t(x)) θ(x)| ≤ ofReal(A) · 1_{B̄_{tR}(y)}(x) · ofReal(θ(x)).

7. (Lintegral bound.) Integrate step 6 over D (lintegral_mono_ae) and pull out the finite constant ofReal(A) (lintegral_const_mul'). The set B := B̄_{tR}(y) is closed, hence measurable, so ∫⁻_D 1_B · g dμ = ∫⁻ g d((μ⌞D)⌞B) = ∫⁻_{B ∩ D} g dμ = ∫⁻_{D ∩ B} g dμ (lintegral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict, Set.inter_comm). Therefore
 ∫⁻_D ofReal|φ(η_t(x)) θ(x)| dμ(x) ≤ ofReal(A) · L(tR).

8. (Bochner bound.) For every function f and set S, |∫_S f dμ| ≤ toReal(∫⁻_S ofReal|f| dμ) (norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm). No integrability is needed: if f is not integrable on S, the left side is 0. Since ofReal(A) · L(tR) < ∞ (step 5), toReal is monotone up to that value (ENNReal.toReal_mono), so step 7 gives
 |∫_D φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ(x)| ≤ toReal(ofReal(A) · L(tR)) = A · toReal(L(tR))
(ENNReal.toReal_mul, and ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with A ≥ 0).

9. (Rescaling.) Since t > 0,
 |(tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_D …| = (tⁿ)⁻¹ |∫_D …| ≤ (tⁿ)⁻¹ · A · toReal(L(tR)).
Moreover toReal(q(tR)) = toReal(L(tR)) / toReal(ofReal((tR)ⁿ)) = toReal(L(tR)) / (tR)ⁿ (ENNReal.toReal_div, and ENNReal.toReal_ofReal since (tR)ⁿ ≥ 0). Also (tR)ⁿ = tⁿ Rⁿ with tⁿ > 0 and Rⁿ > 0. Therefore
 (tⁿ)⁻¹ · A · toReal(L(tR)) = A · Rⁿ · toReal(L(tR)) / (tⁿ Rⁿ) = A · Rⁿ · toReal(q(tR)) = b(t).

10. (Conclusion.) Steps 4–9 show |(tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_D φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ(x)| ≤ b(t) for all sufficiently small t > 0, and b(t) → 0 by step 3(b). By the squeeze theorem, (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_D φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) → 0 as t → 0+. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) and A ≥ 0 with |φ| ≤ A. For t > 0, φ(η_t(x)) = 0 whenever x ∉ B̄_{tR}(y).
Compose the density hypothesis with t ↦ tR, which tends to 0 within (0,∞): q(tR) → 0. Hence eventually q(tR) < ∞ (so L(tR) < ∞), and b(t) := A Rⁿ toReal q(tR) → 0.
Using θ ≥ 0 μ⌞D-a.e. on D (D null-measurable) and measurability of B̄_{tR}(y): ∫⁻_D ofReal|φ(η_t x)θ(x)| ≤ ofReal(A)·L(tR).
norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm and ENNReal.toReal_mono give |∫_D φ(η_t x)θ(x)| ≤ A·toReal L(tR), with no integrability needed.
(tⁿ)⁻¹ A toReal L(tR) = A Rⁿ toReal q(tR) = b(t), and the squeeze theorem gives convergence to 0.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type agree. The density limit yields eventual finiteness of the localized lintegral. Nonnegativity on the null-measurable set gives the required norm bound; indicator integration and finite constant extraction require no measurability of the weight. The unconditional Bochner bound, justified toReal conversion, exact rescaling, and squeeze argument prove the stated limit without integrability or circular assumptions.
